parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime: no trans-specific criminal offence, no documented border, facility or police targeting of visitors, and documented public acceptance (61%). Hate-crime law covering gender identity has been in force since 31 Dec 2024, with an anonymous reporting route. Exposures: rising anti-LGBTQ prejudice (2025 study, not trans-specific); one custodial case with a pending certificate-limitation amendment (first stage only); a single documented custodial record; resident-facing care waits that do not reach visitors. Visitor entry handling of X or mismatched documents and visitor care access are not documented, so they are treated as open questions rather than exposures. Historical state hostility is apologised for (2018). Reduced Risk, below the acceptance-plus-protection tier because of the unresolved custody question and rising prejudice.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented trans-specific border friction, refusals or document-mismatch detentions for visitors. Home-passport gender markers are not checked against domestic regime; X-marker handling is not addressed.
entry_documents.protection: No documented visitor-facing entry restriction; self-declaration regime is resident-facing climate only.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch would route through standard immigration process; no documented escalation to custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: One documented custodial case (trans woman with GRC, convictions/acquittal on threats). Proposed amendment limiting certificate effect 'for purposes of imprisonment' passed first stage only; placement rules for visitors not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Criminal Justice (Hate Offences) Act 2024 applies to custodial and street offences against gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If the amendment passes, certificate-based placement could diverge for those holding recognition; visitors carry home documents, so direct effect is uncertain.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented national facility-exclusion or birth-sex placement rule. Amendment on imprisonment is pending, not enacted.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented facility restriction; 2018 government apology signals institutional repudiation of past hostility.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Single national framework; no subnational facility layer documented.

care_services.exposure: Resident public gender-care waits of 2.5 to 10 years (2022) and reported denials. Minors' gender-affirming care restricted. Visitor access to care not documented.
care_services.protection: Care legal for adults; private sector exists per report.
care_services.interaction: Visitor emergency or continuity care not documented; resident-facing gap does not directly map to visitor exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No current state threat-framing documented. Historical criminalisation until 1993 and 1983 Chief Justice rationale are dated. Residual pension-law hostility is resident-facing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Formal apologies (2018); government-level acknowledgment of past abuse; hate-crime law now operative.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Historical hostility is dated and apologised for; no current enforcement against gender-nonconforming visitors documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Gender-affirming care restricted for minors. 2019 report recommended self-declaration for 16-17 year olds with parental consent; not documented as enacted.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented minor-specific visitor protection; no documented removal of minors from parents.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's care needs would fall under the restricted minors' regime; guardian consent requirements are not documented for visitors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Hate crimes up 15% in 2025 (no denominator; racism and xenophobia dominant). University study (Jul 2025) documents rising anti-LGBTQ prejudice. Local council cancelled a drag event citing abuse (2019).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime law covers gender identity; open public expression, Pride, LGBT venues; 61% public support.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Prejudice rise is not trans-specific violence data; police response to trans victims is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gaps in trans rights and healthcare are acknowledged; employment and housing protections cover sexual orientation only; conversion therapy not banned.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Anonymous online hate-crime reporting form run by a national youth organisation; equality-status links; 2024 hate-offences statute in force.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists for street incidents; efficacy for visitors is not documented. Unverified 2024 report on backing down on hate-speech laws is excluded.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both have no documented traveller-facing trans-specific border or detention exposure and brief-or-none custody risk. This dossier has a documented hate-crime statute and a reporting route, similar to the 0.75-C remedies. It sits similar to 0.75-C on entry but lacks documented visitor-specific remedies, and carries the pending custody amendment, so it is slightly lower.

0.65-E has documented immigration questioning and stalled applications, with remedies that work. This dossier documents no visitor-facing friction, so it sits above 0.65-E on entry. Its unresolved custody question and rising prejudice keep it at or below that tier, not clearly above it.

0.85-D has documented anti-discrimination enforcement with compensation and operative remedies for visitors. This dossier lacks documented enforcement outcomes for trans victims and documents rising prejudice and custody uncertainty, so it sits clearly below 0.85-D.

parsed.synthesis: Protective statute (2024 hate-offences law covering gender identity), documented public acceptance, and no documented visitor-facing trans-specific exclusion or police targeting place this in the Reduced Risk band. Self-declaration is treated as climate signal only. The main exposures are the pending custody-certificate amendment (first stage only) with one documented custodial case, rising anti-LGBTQ prejudice without trans-specific violence figures, and resident care waits that do not reach visitors. Entry handling of X or mismatched documents and visitor care access are open questions, not exposures. Hostile historical policy is apologised for and dated. Remedies exist but their efficacy for visitors is undocumented.
